rationale: Request the first execution for the Node-wrapper proposal question now that the harness has been repaired: the wrapped node is driven through its status channel for every snapshot, the bare leader broadcasts its appends (a bare becomeLeader does not), and the observations are the application-facing Propose outcome plus the leader's own log index around each call. The draft run shows the control passing before the removal and the witness blocked after the re-add with the same leader and term; the attempted leadership-change control is not part of this basis and stays a limitation.

scope.description: Observe the application-facing proposal path of the Node wrapper (Node.Propose) for one wrapped node 2 that is removed from the configuration by leader 1 and then added back by the same leader in the same term, comparing Propose before the removal, after the re-add and with the leader's log index before and after each call.
assumptions: Two voters {1,2} in one process: node 2 is driven through the Node wrapper (newNodeTestHarness, so Readys are consumed and Advance is called) while node 1 is a bare raft instance driven by the harness's message pump; node 1 is made leader directly and broadcasts its appends.

Both nodes apply the removal and the re-add through the application path (n1.applyConfChange and the wrapper's ApplyConfChange), and every snapshot of node 2 is taken through its status channel (node.Status), which is executed inside the run loop.
Propose is called with a 300ms context deadline; a nil proposal channel makes the call return only when that deadline fires.
excluded: A leadership-change control: the draft attempted to restore the channel by campaigning node 2, but that attempt is not part of this basis.

experiment.prefix: Create the wrapped node 2 and a bare node 1 over storages with voters {1,2}; make node 1 leader at term 1 and broadcast its appends; pump messages until node 2 (through its status channel) knows leader 1 and has committed the bootstrap entry; propose through the wrapper and record the outcome; propose the removal of node 2 on node 1, pump, and apply it on both nodes; propose the re-add of node 2 on node 1, pump, and apply it on both nodes; then propose through the wrapper again and record the outcome and the leader's log index around it.
experiment.requirement: Node.Propose is the application-facing proposal path: its documentation states that it proposes data to be appended to the log and warns only that proposals can be lost without notice (node.go:138-140). A node that the application has added back to the configuration, and that knows the leader of that configuration, must therefore be able to hand a proposal to raft - or report why it cannot - rather than block until the caller's context expires while the group never sees the proposal.
experiment.responsibility: raft (target): the wrapper's own bookkeeping decides whether the application's proposals reach the group, and the target's comment at node.go:409-411 records that this bookkeeping is unsound.

comparisons.description: Control: while node 2 is a plain member of {1,2} and knows leader 1, Propose returns without error.
Control: the proposal forwarded by the follower reaches the group - the leader's log index advances.
Premise: after the removal is applied on both nodes, the leader's configuration no longer contains node 2.
Premise: after the re-add is applied on both nodes, the leader's configuration contains node 2 again and node 2 has caught up to the leader's log.
Premise: the wrapped node still knows leader 1 in the same term, so the leadership is unchanged across the removal and the re-add.
Witness: with node 2 a member again and still knowing leader 1, Propose returns only when its context deadline fires (context deadline exceeded after about 300ms).
Witness: the proposal never reached the group - the leader's log index is unchanged across the call.
